lesson: Patch releases lose content silently: v4.1.5 shipped with v4.1.4 absent from history, a 58-line Credit-Aware Routing section attributed to no version, a history entry (v4.1.3 Fable cost caveat) describing a feature the body no longer contains, and Hard Rule 7's enforcement clause dropped. Run specguard.py --spec before accepting any spec revision as source of truth; any 'no open items' claim in Learning Memory must name the version and date it was true for.

Check dispatch against the model-routing table before fan-out. This run's first fan-out put team execution on the orchestrator model (Fable) and was Owner-rejected; the corrected dispatch (Opus units, Fable orchestration gate) ran clean. A pre-dispatch routing check costs one comparison; an Owner interrupt costs the whole fan-out.

Bundling tool-building into a survey unit made it the run's long pole: Discovery took 15.2 min vs 3.7/2.8 for siblings, and orchestrator verification barriered behind it. Split build sub-tasks from survey sub-tasks so verification can start on early returns.
evidence: agent durations in run-journal team_result records

lesson: Multi-file source-of-truth drift: the FOR-CLAUDE package advanced two versions (v4.1.4, v4.1.5) while the SPEC sat at v4.1.3; nothing flagged the divergence until manual review. Every version row must land in every package file in the same patch; specguard needs a cross-file version-sync check (proposed, not built). Corollary: a '(this document)' marker placed before the em dash hid the newest history row from the numbering check — fixed in v4.1.6 by moving the marker after the dash; the newest row is exactly the one that must be machine-checkable.
evidence: v4.1.6 patch cycle 2026-08-17: SPEC before-lint had no v4.1.4/v4.1.5 rows; bounce fix confirmed parseable v4.1.6 rows in both files
